# aeneid-089 — drafter's notes (XI.725–835)

50 units, 111 lines; `t` cut by `A.cut` in `make_units.py`; all script checks pass with no warnings.
Every unit is at most five lines and ends at `. ; : ? !` except two comma cuts where a period runs past five
lines (778–782 `amore,` within 778–784; 785–788 `pruna,` within 785–790). Part name "Tarchon's Rally and the
Death of Camilla (XI.725–835)"; Latin title "Tarcho et Venulus. Mors Camillae". One Greenough paragraph (725);
`p` on unit 725.

## Speech marks
- Tarchon: 732–740 (units 732 … 736, `altos!”`).
- Arruns's prayer to Apollo: 785–793 (units 785 … 792, `urbes.”`).
- Camilla to Acca: opens 823, closes 827 after `Iamque vale.`
- 827 `Iamque vale. ”Simul`: treated as a rule-5b misprint, as 040/041/042 did with the same pattern
  (`domus. ”Et`, `aspicies. ”Dixit`, `parens. ”Sic`): unit `Iamque vale.` gets ” in l and i; unit `”Simul…`
  has it at the head of t, none in l and i; its n opens "The print has 'vale. Simul' with the closing double
  mark joined to 'Simul', a misprint for the mark set straight after 'vale.', corrected here" (worded without
  the ” glyph because the script's DOUBLE MARK IN n check forbids it in n). EXEMPT = {827} (both units start on
  827). Unlike 087's `”Neque` (537), the speech really does end here; only the spacing is wrong.

## Misprints / readings
- No other misprint seen.
- Latin Library variants noted in n: 821 `fida` (would go with `quae`, a different construction, unit 820);
  830 `relinquens` (Camilla lets her arms go vs. her arms leave her, unit 828). 754 `arrectisque` noted as a
  spelling. 728 `inicit` for `incitat` NOT noted: "puts wrath into" vs "stirs up wrath", no real change of
  sense — reviewer may disagree.
- 768 `Cybelo` taken as dative of the mountain Cybelus (some texts `Cybelae`, from memory).
- 760 `iaculo` taken with `circuit` (alternative with `velocem` mentioned); `prior` with Arruns.
- 738 `exspectate` taken as scornful imperative.
- 822 `quicum partiri curas` explained as compressed, `erat` understood; construction doubtful, a reviewer
  with Conington to hand may want to check (from memory).

## Attributions from memory (unchecked)
- Iliad X.68–69 (calling each man by name), Iliad IV/V rebukes, Iliad XII.200–207 (eagle and snake),
  Iliad XVI.249–252 (Zeus grants half of Achilles' prayer), Iliad XV.586–590 (Antilochus like a beast),
  Iliad XXI.70 (spear eager for flesh), Herodotus I.94 (Lydian origin of Etruscans), Pliny the Elder on the
  Hirpi Sorani walking on coals, V.438 `tela exit`, XI.591–592 (Diana's curse on Camilla's killer),
  VIII.9 / XI.242–295 (Venulus's embassy), IX.359–374 (Euryalus and the helmet).
